title: Use `raw_path` for the request target in access logs
author: feiiiiii5

spotlights.label: Only double quotes are escaped now
spotlights.why: quote() used to percent-encode every character outside its safe set. h11 accepts any printable ASCII in the target, so GET /a<b> used to log /a%3Cb%3E and now logs /a<b>; the same goes for \ { } | ^ and backticks. Whitespace and control bytes still cannot reach the log, because the parsers reject them.

spotlights.label: Quotes in the query string now become %22
spotlights.why: Before, the query string was appended verbatim, so ?a"b put a bare quote inside the quoted request field. The final replace() now covers the query too. A fix, but a logged query changes for anyone grepping for it.

spotlights.label: In-place path rewrites no longer reach the log
spotlights.why: The log line is written at http.response.start from the same scope dict the app received. An app or middleware that rewrote scope["path"] in place used to change the logged path; raw_path is rarely touched, so the log now shows the wire target whatever the app did.

spotlights.label: A scope without raw_path now raises KeyError
spotlights.why: The PR reads scope["raw_path"] with no fallback, on purpose. Every uvicorn protocol sets it, but any outside code calling get_path_with_query_string with a hand-built scope that lacks it will now fail instead of logging.

spotlights.label: WebSocket log lines have no new test
spotlights.why: The three WebSocket implementations call the same function for their accept and reject log lines, and they all set raw_path, but the new tests only drive HTTP. The quote test also skips zttp, which rejects quotes in the target.

steps.title: Log the request target as the client sent it
steps.why: get_path_with_query_string() stops re-encoding the decoded scope["path"] with urllib.parse.quote() and decodes scope["raw_path"] as latin1 instead. The query string is appended as before, then every double quote in the result becomes %22.
steps.consequence: Every HTTP and WebSocket access line names the target the client sent: /one%2Ftwo stays /one%2Ftwo and /%41 stays /%41, with the --root-path prefix still in front.

notes: Now covers the query string too

steps.title: Prove encoded targets and quotes log unchanged
steps.why: test_request_logging gains /one%2Ftwo and /%41, and still asserts the logged target equals the sent one. A new test sends /foo"bar?a"b and expects both quotes logged as %22.
steps.consequence: Every HTTP protocol class is pinned to log the sent target; zttp is skipped for the quote case, and WebSocket logging is not exercised.

notes: Logged target must equal the sent one
pytest.skip("zttp rejects quotes in the request target")
